task.description: WF-02 Step 5 for REQ-134: independently re-run scripts/test_parallel.sh (do not trust TEST-RUNNER's report alone), confirm every acceptance criterion against actual code/tests, check docs/requirements.yaml and docs/status/ for staleness.
acceptance_criteria: a test obtains a genuine token from the running Keycloak and drives it through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline end to end, with the real assertion output quoted
the token's signature is verified against the live JWKS via the real verifier, not TokenVerifierDouble -- demonstrated by the test failing if pointed at a tampered token
JIT provisioning creates a real user row on first authentication and reuses it on the second, asserted across two calls
the default mix test run still passes with Keycloak stopped, quoted as evidence
the real-token tests skip with a message naming exactly what must be running, rather than failing obscurely
the result states the exact command a developer runs to execute them

result.summary:
Independent re-verification of REQ-134 on feature/WF02-REQ134-20260823 at commit 19cb050 (git pull: already up to date). Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's step4 report -- re-ran the suite myself three separate ways and read every shipped artifact directly.

1. Full default suite, own re-run: `TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 scripts/test_parallel.sh` -> 'combined: 1981 tests, 5 properties, 0 failures (1986/1986 passed)', all 4 partitions clean (472/451/521/537 tests, 0/0/0/0 failures). Matches TEST-RUNNER's attempt-2 total exactly, but independently derived, not copied.

2. Live-Keycloak suite, own re-run (3rd independent execution overall, after TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's and TEST-RUNNER's): `mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs` against letflow-keycloak-1 (port 8093, realm bpm-default, already healthy) -> 'Result: 3 passed', 0 failures.

3. AC4, re-derived under the actual condition it is about (core-directives.md's 'Re-derive under the conditions the property is actually about'): every prior gate's AC4 evidence was gathered with Keycloak RUNNING, inferring pass-with-Keycloak-down only from the exclusion mechanism being config-static. That is not proof the whole app/suite still boots and passes when Keycloak is genuinely unreachable -- Letflow.Application unconditionally starts an Oidcc.ProviderConfiguration.Worker against the real issuer (lib/letflow/application.ex:17-35, pre-existing from REQ-128, not part of this diff) regardless of :token_verifier, so a synchronous-connect worker could in principle have blocked app/test-suite startup entirely with Keycloak down -- a real failure mode AC4's wording is specifically guarding against. So I ran `docker compose stop keycloak`, confirmed via docker compose ps it was stopped, then ran plain `mix test` (no partitions, no --include) end to end: 'Result: 1986 passed (5 properties, 1981 tests), 3 excluded', 0 failures, in 922.3s. This is real evidence AC4 holds under the literal condition the AC names, not merely evidence the exclusion mechanism is static. Restarted Keycloak afterward (`docker compose start keycloak`, confirmed healthy again) to leave the environment as found.

4. AC-by-AC code verification (read test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs and test/support/keycloak_test_client.ex directly, not TEST-RUNNER's summary):
   AC1 -- lines 211-228: KeycloakTestClient.direct_access_token/4 obtains a real token, call_pipeline_with_token/1 drives it through AuthPipeline.call/2, asserts conn not halted and conn.assigns.auth_context matches {tenant_id, user_id: binary, roles containing "PLATFORM_ADMIN"}. Real assertion output quoted in test/reports/report-20260823-WF02-REQ134-20260823-attempt2.yaml and reconfirmed by my own re-run (3 passed). SATISFIED.
   AC2 -- keycloak_test_client.ex:138-158 tamper_signature/1 flips every byte of the signature segment (guaranteed-different, ArgumentError guard on malformed input); test lines 235-256 drive the tampered token through the SAME AuthPipeline.call/2 under the real Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc override (setup at lines 108-121, not TokenVerifierDouble -- TokenVerifierDouble has no tamper concept at all), asserting conn.halted, conn.status == 401, and a partial match on %{"error" => "unauthorized"}. This demonstrates the real verifier's live-JWKS signature check is load-bearing, not a pass-through. SATISFIED.
   AC3 -- test lines 262-303: count-before (reset via reset_subject_row!/2, scoped by prefix: schema_name -- schema-per-tenant, cannot touch another tenant's data) == 0, first AuthPipeline.call/2 -> count == 1, second call with the SAME token -> user_id_1 == user_id_2 and count still == 1. The identity check (not just the count) is the required proof against a delete-then-reinsert false positive. SATISFIED.
   AC4 -- SATISFIED, and now with strictly better evidence than any prior gate: real `mix test` output with Keycloak container literally stopped, quoted above, 1986/1986 passed / 3 excluded, 0 failures.
   AC5 -- test/test_helper.exs:9 excludes :keycloak by default; the module's setup_all (lines 83-100) probes discovery reachability and, on failure, raises a plain RuntimeError with the exact text 'Keycloak not ready at <url>. Ensure docker-compose services are running (docker compose up -d keycloak) before executing these tests.' (line 93-94, quoted verbatim from the file). Sanity-checked per the dispatch instructions: this message genuinely names both what's down (Keycloak, with the exact discovery URL) and what to do about it (the exact docker compose command) -- it is the first and only thing a developer sees. The deviation from the design's literal {:skip, message} is real (ExUnit 1.20.3's setup_all does not accept that return shape, verified directly in the moduledoc's own quoted measurement) and was already independently reviewed and ruled compliant-in-spirit by REVIEWER (step2d), correctly on substance: AC5's text is about the developer-facing outcome (clear, targeted message vs. an obscure one), not which internal ExUnit counter increments. Concur with that judgement -- SATISFIED. REVIEWER also filed a MINOR non-blocking issue that lib/letflow/design/req134-real-keycloak-token-integration.md S3.1 still describes the old {:skip, message} mechanism and should be corrected at the source; carrying that forward below as a DOC-UPDATER note, not a blocker.
   AC6 -- the test module's moduledoc (lines 11-13) states the exact command verbatim: `mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs`, matching every gate's quoted evidence including my own re-run above. SATISFIED.

5. Staleness check: docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-134 entry is status: in_progress -- correct pre-Step-6, not stale (confirmed against the dispatch note). docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml names volume 4 (docs/status/requirement_status.v4.yaml) as current; grepped it directly and found exactly one REQ-134 event so far -- a 'started' event at 2026-08-23T10:43:56Z from Step 00 -- and no 'done' event, which is correct since Step 6 has not run yet. Nothing stale found.

6. git diff main...HEAD --stat: 18 files changed, zero lib/ application code (only lib/letflow/design/req134-real-keycloak-token-integration.md, a design doc), matching the design's own stated scope (no ELIXIR-DEV involvement, correctly skipped).

Overall: all 6 acceptance criteria independently confirmed against the actual shipped code and my own freshly-obtained test evidence, not against any prior report's summary. No blocking issue found.

issues.description: Carried forward from REVIEWER's step2d finding, not newly discovered here: lib/letflow/design/req134-real-keycloak-token-integration.md S3.1 still describes setup_all returning {:skip, message}, which this repo's installed ExUnit (1.20.3) does not support -- the shipped test correctly raises RuntimeError with the intended message text instead. Recommend DOC-UPDATER correct S3.1 to describe the raise-with-exact-message mechanism as part of REQ-134's close-out, so a future reader of the design doc doesn't re-derive the same investigation.
